findings.title: Availability not stated on inspected product pages
priorityReasons: "product.availability" is a tier 2 field (affects how a found product presents).
It applies to 12 of the 12 inspected pages in this sample.
Tier 2 at this share of the sample gives priority "high".
findings.metric: An availability status was stated on 0 of 12 inspected product pages.
findings.finding: No stock or availability status was stated on 12 of the 12 inspected product pages.
findings.impact: Buyers cannot tell from the page whether an item can be supplied, which moves the question to a phone call.
findings.recommendation: Publish an availability status on each product page, even where the value is "made to order" or "on request".

findings.title: Brand not stated on inspected product pages
priorityReasons: "product.brand" is a tier 2 field (affects how a found product presents).
It applies to 12 of the 12 inspected pages in this sample.
Tier 2 at this share of the sample gives priority "high".
findings.metric: A brand was stated on 0 of 12 inspected product pages.
findings.finding: No brand or manufacturer was stated in structured data or in a labelled field on 12 of the 12 inspected product pages.
findings.impact: Buyers searching for a specific manufacturer cannot narrow to it, and brand facets cannot be built from those pages.
findings.recommendation: State the brand in a structured field on each product page, not only in the product title.

findings.title: Dimensional data not present on inspected product pages
priorityReasons: "product.dimensions" is a tier 1 field (needed to find and filter a product).
It applies to 11 of the 12 inspected pages in this sample.
Tier 1 at this share of the sample gives priority "high".
findings.metric: Dimensional data was observed on 1 of 12 inspected product pages.
findings.finding: No dimensional attribute (width, height, length, depth, diameter or an explicit size) was found on 11 of the 12 inspected product pages.
findings.impact: Buyers who need to confirm fit cannot do so on the page, and dimensional filters cannot be offered for those products.
findings.recommendation: Record dimensions as separate named attributes with their units, rather than only inside prose or an image.

findings.title: Weight not present on inspected product pages
priorityReasons: "product.weight" is a tier 1 field (needed to find and filter a product).
It applies to 11 of the 12 inspected pages in this sample.
Tier 1 at this share of the sample gives priority "high".
findings.metric: A weight attribute was observed on 1 of 12 inspected product pages.
findings.finding: No weight or mass attribute was found on 11 of the 12 inspected product pages.
findings.impact: Shipping and handling questions cannot be answered from the page, and weight-based delivery rules have nothing to read.
findings.recommendation: Publish weight as a named attribute with its unit on each product page.

findings.title: Specifications not present on inspected product pages
priorityReasons: "product.specifications" is a tier 1 field (needed to find and filter a product).
It applies to 11 of the 12 inspected pages in this sample.

findings.metric: A specification block was observed on 1 of 12 inspected product pages.
findings.finding: A specification block (a table, definition list, or labelled key/value list) could not be found on 11 of the 12 inspected product pages.
findings.impact: A buyer comparing options on those pages has nothing structured to compare, and the pages carry no attribute data for a search or filter to index.
findings.recommendation: Publish a consistent specification block on each product page, using the same attribute names across the range so the values can be compared and filtered.

findings.title: Inspected product pages carrying no descriptive or attribute data
priorityReasons: "product.attributes" is a tier 1 field (needed to find and filter a product).

currentContent.summary: This review covers 15 page(s) inspected on https://jamescotrading.com/, of which 12 were product pages and 2 were category pages. 8 product-data finding(s) were recorded, each traceable to a specific page and source fragment.
currentContent.headline: Product Data Health Check — Jamesco Trading Ltd
currentContent.nextStep: Review these findings against the pages cited, and confirm whether the same gaps hold across the wider catalogue. AltiusNXT can then scope what it would take to close them.
currentContent.scopeNote: Scope: this audit inspected a bounded sample and stopped at maxPages (15), frontier not exhausted. Every figure describes the inspected pages only and should not be read as a measure of the whole catalogue.

businessPain.observation: A specification block (a table, definition list, or labelled key/value list) could not be found on 11 of the 12 inspected product pages.
businessPain.businessPain: Buyers comparing similar parts may not find the same technical detail on each one, so the comparison has to happen off the site — in a datasheet, or on the phone.
businessPain.whyItMatters: Industrial buyers select on specification. Where a specification is absent, the product is hard to choose with confidence even when it is the right part.
businessPain.potentialOpportunity: Holding specifications as named attributes rather than prose lets the same values drive filtering, comparison and export to a marketplace.
businessPain.recommendedDirection: Agree a specification set per product family, then populate it from the sources that already hold the values.

businessPain.observation: No brand or manufacturer was stated in structured data or in a labelled field on 12 of the 12 inspected product pages.
businessPain.businessPain: Brand was not consistently stated on the inspected product pages, so buyers who search by manufacturer may not find the product.
businessPain.whyItMatters: In distribution, brand is one of the first filters a buyer reaches for. A product without it is effectively outside that path.
businessPain.potentialOpportunity: A consistent brand attribute supports brand-led navigation and makes catalogue coverage visible by supplier.
businessPain.recommendedDirection: Normalise brand to a controlled list rather than free text.

businessPain.observation: No dimensional attribute (width, height, length, depth, diameter or an explicit size) was found on 11 of the 12 inspected product pages.
businessPain.businessPain: Dimensions were not consistently available on the inspected product pages, so a buyer checking fit has to look elsewhere.
businessPain.whyItMatters: Fit is often the deciding question, and it is one of the few a buyer cannot resolve by judgement.
businessPain.potentialOpportunity: Recording dimensions as separate named values with their units makes them filterable and reusable across channels.
businessPain.recommendedDirection: Capture dimensions as structured attributes with an explicit unit, per product family.

businessPain.observation: No weight or mass attribute was found on 11 of the 12 inspected product pages.
businessPain.businessPain: Weight was not consistently present, which affects both shipping expectations and handling decisions.
businessPain.whyItMatters: Weight drives freight cost and handling requirements, so its absence moves a question downstream.
businessPain.potentialOpportunity: A populated weight attribute supports shipping calculation and marketplace requirements.
businessPain.recommendedDirection: Populate weight with a stated unit as part of the core attribute set.

businessPain.observation: 6 of the 12 inspected product pages carried none of: specifications, attributes, dimensions, weight, brand, or a description.
businessPain.businessPain: Page-level metadata was incomplete on the inspected pages, which affects how the page is represented when it appears elsewhere.
businessPain.whyItMatters: Metadata is what a page looks like before anyone has visited it.
businessPain.potentialOpportunity: Metadata derived from the product record stays correct as the catalogue changes.
businessPain.recommendedDirection: Generate page metadata from product attributes rather than maintaining it separately.

businessPain.observation: No product description was found in structured data or a description field on 7 of the 12 inspected product pages.
businessPain.businessPain: Descriptions on the inspected pages carried little distinguishing information, so similar products read alike.
businessPain.whyItMatters: A description is where a buyer confirms they have understood the product. Thin text moves that confirmation to a phone call.
businessPain.potentialOpportunity: Descriptions built from the product attributes stay accurate as the data changes and read consistently across the range.
businessPain.recommendedDirection: Generate descriptions from the attribute set, with a human review step, rather than writing each one independently.

businessPain.observation: No Product schema (JSON-LD or microdata) was declared on 1 of the 12 inspected product pages.
businessPain.businessPain: The inspected product pages did not publish machine-readable product markup, so systems that read the page have to infer its content.
businessPain.whyItMatters: Search engines, AI assistants and marketplace integrations all read structured markup. Without it they interpret the page as prose.
businessPain.potentialOpportunity: Publishing structured product data from the attributes that already exist makes the same content readable by machines.
businessPain.recommendedDirection: Emit product structured data generated from the product record, not hand-maintained.

businessPain.observation: No stock or availability status was stated on 12 of the 12 inspected product pages.
businessPain.businessPain: Availability was not consistently shown, so a buyer cannot tell whether an item can be supplied without asking.
businessPain.whyItMatters: Availability is often the difference between an order placed now and an enquiry that waits.
businessPain.potentialOpportunity: Surfacing the stock position already held in the source system removes that question.
businessPain.recommendedDirection: Publish availability from the existing stock record, at whatever granularity is defensible.

businessValue.nextStep: A 15-minute walkthrough covers what was found, what it would take to address, and what a worked example looks like on your own products.
businessValue.financialNote: Potential opportunity — not quantified in this audit. This review observed product data on a bounded sample of pages. It did not measure sales, traffic or cost, and nothing here should be read as a projection of any of them.
businessValue.whatWeObserved: We inspected 15 page(s) on the Jamesco Trading Ltd website, 12 of them product pages, and recorded 8 product-data finding(s). 6 of them affect fields a buyer needs in order to find and filter a product.
businessValue.whyThisMatters: Industrial buyers select on specification. Where a specification is absent, the product is hard to choose with confidence even when it is the right part. In distribution, brand is one of the first filters a buyer reaches for. A product without it is effectively outside that path. Fit is often the deciding question, and it is one of the few a buyer cannot resolve by judgement.
businessValue.improvedExperience: The improved position is a product page where the specifications, identifiers and availability a buyer needs are each present as named values — filterable, comparable, and readable by the systems that list them elsewhere.
businessValue.howAltiusNxtCanHelp: AltiusNXT works on the product record itself: agreeing the attribute set for each product family, populating it from the sources that already hold the values, and publishing it in a form both buyers and systems can read. The audit points at where to start.
businessValue.whereThePainMayAppear: Buyers comparing similar parts may not find the same technical detail on each one, so the comparison has to happen off the site — in a datasheet, or on the phone. Brand was not consistently stated on the inspected product pages, so buyers who search by manufacturer may not find the product. Dimensions were not consistently available on the inspected product pages, so a buyer checking fit has to look elsewhere.

businessImpact: A buyer comparing options on those pages has nothing structured to compare, and the pages carry no attribute data for a search or filter to index.
Buyers searching for a specific manufacturer cannot narrow to it, and brand facets cannot be built from those pages.
Buyers who need to confirm fit cannot do so on the page, and dimensional filters cannot be offered for those products.
Shipping and handling questions cannot be answered from the page, and weight-based delivery rules have nothing to read.
Those pages identify a product by name and little else, so a buyer cannot evaluate the item and a search engine has nothing specific to index against it.

discoverability.observation: Specifications not present on inspected product pages: 1 of 12 inspected product pages.
discoverability.consideration: Specification questions are answered from named attributes. Where specifications sit only in prose, they are harder for any system to extract reliably.

discoverability.observation: Inspected product pages carrying no descriptive or attribute data: 6 of 12 inspected product pages.
discoverability.consideration: Page metadata determines how a page is represented in a result list. Incomplete metadata was observed on the inspected pages.

discoverability.observation: Product description not present on inspected product pages: 5 of 12 inspected product pages.
discoverability.consideration: Where similar products carry similar text, there is little to distinguish the pages from one another. This is a potential discoverability consideration observed on the inspected pages.

discoverability.observation: Product description not present on inspected product pages: 5 of 12 inspected product pages.
discoverability.consideration: A question-answering system needs distinguishing detail to match a product to a question. Thin descriptions offer little to match on.

discoverability.observation: Product structured data not declared on inspected product pages: 11 of 12 inspected product pages.
discoverability.consideration: Search engines read product markup to understand what a page describes. Without it, a product page is interpreted as ordinary text — a potential discoverability consideration, not a measured ranking effect.

discoverability.observation: Product structured data not declared on inspected product pages: 11 of 12 inspected product pages.
discoverability.consideration: Assistants answering a product question draw on structured data where it exists. Its absence means any answer has to be inferred from prose.

discoverability.observation: Product structured data not declared on inspected product pages: 11 of 12 inspected product pages.
discoverability.consideration: Systems that summarise products for a generated answer rely on machine-readable attributes. Unstructured pages give them less to work with.

recommendedImprovementAreas: Publish a consistent specification block on each product page, using the same attribute names across the range so the values can be compared and filtered.
State the brand in a structured field on each product page, not only in the product title.
Record dimensions as separate named attributes with their units, rather than only inside prose or an image.
Publish weight as a named attribute with its unit on each product page.
Establish a minimum data set that a product page must carry before it is published, and backfill the pages that fall short of it.

providerResults.reason: LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN is not set. LinkedIn person data requires an approved LinkedIn Partner Program application; there is no self-service credential. Third-party LinkedIn scraper Actors ARE reachable from the configured Apify account and were deliberately NOT used, because scraping LinkedIn without authorisation violates its terms whether done directly or through an intermediary.

APOLLO_API_KEY is not set. No Apollo.io account or API credential exists in this environment, and Apollo people-search data is not obtainable without one. Apollo data reachable via third-party scrapers was NOT used, because that bypasses the provider paywall.

No ZoomInfo credentials are set (needs ZOOMINFO_USERNAME with either ZOOMINFO_PASSWORD, or ZOOMINFO_CLIENT_ID + ZOOMINFO_PRIVATE_KEY for PKI auth). ZoomInfo has no self-service API tier: access requires an enterprise contract, so this cannot be unblocked by signing up.
ROCKETREACH_API_KEY is not set. No RocketReach account exists in this environment, and its person-search API requires a paid plan.
None of the 6 standard team-page paths on jamescotrading.com could be reached.
